correctness.rationale: For the lifted walk, coverage of the cycle occurs precisely when the visited integer range reaches width \(n-1\). With \(b=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\), the probability \(K>b\) is \(r^{b+1}\); the strong Markov property after hitting \(b\) bounds any later new minimum by another \(r^{b+1}\). On the good event coverage occurs exactly at \(H_{n-1-K}\), at vertex \(n-1-K\), giving the claimed joint error bound for all \(n\ge3\) and \(p\in(1/2,1)\). Unit-upcrossing times have finite exponential moments, mean \(1/(p-q)\), and variance \(4pq/(p-q)^3\). Their classical central limit theorem, the tight difference between cover and passage times, and a finite-prefix conditional Gaussian limit establish the independent Gaussian–geometric joint law. The standalone verify.py passed 331210 exact/deterministic path assertions, which supplement rather than substitute for this infinite proof.

value.rationale: Cycle exploration risk is two-dimensional: where the final unexplored location lies and how long exploration takes. The recent arXiv:2610.15115 establishes only the last-site marginal, while the theorem gives an exponentially reliable joint pathwise representation with an exact finite-n mismatch bound, plus independent Gaussian–geometric asymptotics and conditional time limits.
